newsitem.title: CHINA: China March industrial output up 13.5 percent.
newsitem.headline: China March industrial output up 13.5 percent.

text.p: China's industrial output for the first quarter rose by 11.0 percent year-on-year while output in March alone was up by 13.5 percent, the State Statistical Bureau said on Tuesday.
Total output value was 452.5 billion yuan in the first quarter, the bureau said.
The increase in industrial output value slowed in the first quarter compared with the year-ago period, although output accelerated in March from 10.4 percent in the first two months.
Wholly owned state industry and industry in which the state has a majority stake showed output value growth of 6.8 percent in the first quarter, with state industry alone growing by 5.1 percent.
Collective industry showed output growth of 12.1 percent, with output of rural township enteprises up by 13.5 percent.
However, that represented a sharp slowdown compared with the year-ago period, the bureau said.
Output growth of foreign-funded firms, stock-holding enterprises and private enteprise was rather fast, up by 14.7 percent, the bureau said.
Light and heavy industry output showed a better response to market factors, the bureau said.
Light industrial output value in the first quarter reached 190.3 billion yuan, up by 11.2 percent year-on-year. Output of heavy industry rose by 10.9 percent to 262.2 billion yuan.
Production of consumer goods was rather fast, it said.

Output of colour televisions, radios, cameras, washing machines, refrigerators, freezers and air conditioners increased by between 12.7 percent and 33.6 percent. Production of beer soared by 11.5 percent and beverages output was up by 25.5 percent.
Production of primary energy in the first quarter totalled 291 million tonnes, up by 5.1 percent year-on-year.
Coal output rose 5.4 percent to 310 million tonnes while crude production was up 2.9 percent to 40 million tonnes.
Steel and steel products rose between 4.3 and 8.3 percent.
The bureau cited some positive changes in Chinese industry in the first quarter, but said several outstanding problems remained.
A large number of companies faced production and management difficulties, with some state enterprises facing particularly serious problems, the bureau said.
The next step was to speed up state enterprise reform, reversing losses and boosting profits as well as quality, it said. It did not say how this target was to be achieved.
